title.narrative: Strengthen Associations of Local Authorities at national, regional and global levels

description.narrative: The European Commission decided in 2015 to engage at political level with five Global and Regional Associations of Local Authorities (ALAs). This was the result of a worldwide structured dialogue with CSOs and LAs held in 2010/2011 and the Communication from the Commission (2013) ¿Empowering LAs in partner countries for enhanced governance and more effective development outcomes¿.The commitment translated in the signature for a six years period (2015-2020) of strategic Framework Partnership Agreements (FPAs) with: United Cities and Local Government (UCLG), the International Association of Francophone Mayors (AIMF), the Commonwealth Local Government Forum (CLGF), United Cities and Local Governments of Africa (UCLG-A), and the Council of European Municipalities and Regions (CEMR)/PLATFORMA. These strategic partnerships that will be renewed in 2021, are accompanied by financial commitments from the Commission through five Specific Grant Agreements (SGAs) covering the new programming period 2021-2027. This proposed Action for 2021 will ensure the continuation of the partnerships established through the FPAs for the period 2021-2027 in line with the LAs component of the Multi-Annual Indicative thematic Programme for ¿Global Challenges¿.The overall objective of the Action is to contribute to further improve the enabling environment for Local Authorities by supporting the improvement of multi-level governance through partnerships with United Cities and Local Governments of Africa (UCLG-A)and United Cities and Local Governments (UCLG), in line with the European Commission¿s commitment to work towards ensuring a truly inclusive multilateralism, where the voices of civil society, the private sector, social partners and local authorities count (Communication on strengthening the EU¿s contribution to rules-based multilateralism).In particular it will aim to increase their transparency, accountability, advocacy capacities and empowermentalso in multilateral settings. The ALAs will be allowed to play their role and to contribute to policy-making on the development agenda (e.g. Policy Forum for Development) and policy implementation processes in particular in relation to the localisation of the SDGs.This should result in the increased institutional, operational and financial sustainability of ALAs; the strengthening of theircapacities and those of their members; the enhancement of the coordination between ALAs;an increase oftheir capacities to impact and contribute to regional and global policy-making processes on development for the localisation of SDGs. The action will contribute to and develop synergies with Team Europe Initiatives focusing on decentralisation and urban interventions (including sustainable cities) as well as those falling into the realm where local authorities and ALAs have key competences, e.g. water and sanitation, education, health, climate change, environment, migration, and local economic development.
